$comment: Where each stored source came from, and what its published pages looked like when a person last confirmed them.
A SIDECAR, NOT A HEADER IN THE FILES. The vendored sources are evidence: `provenance-honesty.test.ts` pins
each one's digest so that a verification date is bound to the exact bytes that were verified — 'it proves the
bytes have not moved since they said they did'. Writing our own metadata into those files moves the bytes and
forces a re-pin, which breaks the binding the invariant exists to protect. An earlier draft of this did exactly
that and four of those tests failed, which is the invariant working.
`pages` IS A LIST BECAUSE THE SOURCES ARE NOT ONE PAGE. FL-Stat consolidates six statute sections; CT, UT and
both Virginia form extractions cite two each. A consolidation is watched by watching its parts, and any part is
the law — so a source counts as checkable only once EVERY page has a confirmed baseline. Checking the parts
somebody got to and ignoring the rest would report 'unchanged' for a statute with an unwatched section.
`digest` IS NULL UNTIL A PERSON READS THE PAGE. It records what the published page hashed to when someone
confirmed it is the statute we stored. A machine taking that baseline on its first run would hash the page
against itself and silently bless an amendment nobody had seen, so recording one is a person's job and until
they do the source is reported as needing a person.
The URLs are NOT looked up. Each is recorded in the source's own header, in the 2026-09-12 source audit's
verified retrieval, or in that document's text sibling — the `note` on each entry says which.
